title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps

epigraph.quote: A multiple never tells you whether a stock is cheap or expensive until you know how much future cash flow is already baked into today’s price.
epigraph.author: Institutional Valuation Principle

web_blocks.title: What ₹277.00 (2026-11-23 Ledger) and ₹268.10 (2026-11-25 Live TV) Price In

web_blocks.html: On the verified 2026-11-23 NSE ledger close, Kross Limited traded at ₹277.00 (down 15.13% from its ₹326.40 52-week high) [33]. By the 2026-11-25 live TradingView snapshot, shares slipped another 3.21% to ₹268.10, putting market capitalization at ₹1,789.49 Cr [33]. At ₹268.10, Kross trades at 24.91x trailing twelve-month earnings and 3.31x book value, down from 28.42x P/E at ₹305.90 on November 13, 2026 [23][33]. That pullback erased part of the post-Q2 FY27 rally after sales jumped +79.6% YoY to ₹235.1 Cr and PAT surged +143.5% YoY to ₹19.69 Cr [3][30].

A Reverse DCF shows why the market still prices in strong execution. Forward enterprise value sits near ₹1,955 Cr once we add guided March 2027 gross debt of ~₹165–170 Cr [29]. Debt rises from ₹119 Cr in September 2026 as Kross draws its remaining ~₹50 Cr term loan for ~₹110 Cr H2 capex [29][30]. At a 12.5% cost of capital and 5.0% terminal growth rate, ₹268.10–₹277.00 implies 14%–16% annual sales growth through FY32 [1][33]. It also assumes EBITDA margins rise from 12.06% TTM toward 14.5%–15.0%, with working capital under 95 days [1][29][33].

Our November 2026 Pass 1 audit requires trimming FY28E fair-value targets. Three new facts weigh on free cash flow and return on capital. First, H1 FY27 CFO fell to ₹4.73 Cr (14.3% of ₹33.16 Cr PAT) after a ₹23.89 Cr jump in Other Current Assets [30]. That yielded -₹54.43 Cr H1 FCF on top of -₹111 Cr across FY24–FY26 [11][30]. Second, the Oct 30 preferential issue brought only ₹39.75 Cr upfront, with ₹23.85 Cr tied to 18-month promoter warrants across 6.75 Cr diluted shares [32]. Debt must bridge H2 capex plus a new ₹20–25 Cr Cold Drawn Tube line [29]. Third, selling the ~50% non-captive surplus of 1,20,000 TPA Mill 219 pits Kross against a 93%-share domestic oligopoly (Maharashtra Seamless, Jindal SAW, Kirloskar Ferrous/ISMT) with zero Oil & Gas track record [31].

web_blocks.takeaway: Trimming Base Case FY28E PAT from ₹108 Cr to ₹101 Cr (₹14.96 diluted EPS across 6.75 Cr shares) and Exit P/E from 25.0x to 24.0x yields a ₹360.00 Base Target. Against our ratcheted ₹219.06 hard stop, Base Case R:R is 1.43:1 at the 2026-11-23 NSE close (₹277.00), 1.87:1 at the 2026-11-25 live TV close (₹268.10), and 3.28:1 at the ₹252.00 top of our ₹234.00–₹252.00 support entry zone.

web_blocks.title: Head-to-Head Peer Comps: Growth Premium vs. Capital-Efficiency Gap

web_blocks.html: Live 2026-11-25 TradingView peer comps sharpen the valuation boundary [34]. Jamna Auto trades at 21.70x TTM P/E with 22.48% ROE, 0.01x debt-to-equity, and 12.81% OPM [34]. GNA Axles trades at 15.49x TTM P/E with 14.40% ROE, 0.19x debt-to-equity, and +23.06% TTM revenue growth [34]. Ramkrishna Forgings trades at 73.46x TTM P/E on compressed 8.69% OPM and 5.61% ROE [34]. Bharat Forge sits in Stage 4 at 121.51x TTM P/E after a -36.88% TTM EPS drop and 6.55% ROE [34].

web_blocks.caption: Indian CV, Axle & Forging Peer Comparison (Verified 2026-11-25 Live TradingView Snapshot)
web_blocks.takeaway: At 24.91x TTM P/E (₹268.10 live TV close), Kross still commands a premium to both Jamna Auto (21.70x P/E, 22.48% ROE, 0.01x D/E) and GNA Axles (15.49x P/E, 14.40% ROE) because Kross delivers +35.86% TTM sales growth and +40.17% EPS growth—yet its 14.3% H1 FY27 CFO/PAT conversion caps our FY28E multiple at 24.0x.

web_blocks.company: GNA Axles Ltd (FY18–FY20 Commercial Vehicle & Tractor Cycle)
web_blocks.mechanism: Like Kross, GNA Axles entered a truck upcycle with strong OEM approvals and new capacity. When US Class 8 builds and Indian M&HCV sales cooled in FY19–FY20, sales and margins fell together and its P/E shrank.
web_blocks.outcome_numbers: GNA Axles fell over 55% from its 2018 peak to its 2020 low as P/E dropped from ~22x to single digits. By November 25, 2026, it trades at 15.49x TTM P/E on ₹2,259.23 Cr market cap and 14.40% ROE.
web_blocks.lesson_for_symbol: Peak earnings times peak P/E multiples create sharp downside when freight slows. Demanding a 15.5x Bear multiple and buying only near structural support guards against simultaneous margin and multiple compression.

web_blocks.html: Our 24.0x Base Case exit multiple—a modest premium to Jamna Auto’s 21.70x and well above GNA Axles’ 15.49x—is explicitly conditional on captive Mill 219 integration lifting EBITDA margins by +125–150 bps and restoring ROCE toward 19%–20% [34]. We refuse to assign a 30x+ compounder multiple while Kross funds -₹54.43 Cr H1 FCF with term debt heading to ~₹165–170 Cr and faces three entrenched incumbents holding 93% of Indian seamless tube supply [29][30][31].

Valuation Decision Trigger: Base Case fair value is trimmed from ₹400.00 to ₹360.00 (24.0x FY28E diluted EPS of ₹14.96). New capital waits for ₹234.00–₹252.00 (3.28:1 R:R from ₹252.00 against our ratcheted ₹219.06 hard stop) paired with Q3 FY27 cash-conversion proof or clean Feb–Mar 2027 Mill 219 trials.

book_paragraphs: For six chapters, you and I deliberately kept the stock quote out of sight while auditing Kross Limited’s five Jamshedpur plants, its single-piece extruded trailer axles, and its newly uncovered balance-sheet strains. Now we bring the stock price back onto the desk—and we must read two distinct timestamps with precision. On the verified November 23, 2026 NSE ledger close, Kross traded at ₹277.00. Two sessions later, on the live November 25, 2026 TradingView snapshot, shares slipped another 3.21% to ₹268.10, valuing the business at ₹1,789.49 Cr, or 24.91x trailing earnings and 3.31x book value.

That 12.54% one-month pullback from our November 13 review price of ₹305.90 has cooled the valuation multiple from 28.42x down to 24.91x. Yet a cheaper stock price does not automatically make a bargain if the underlying cash-flow and debt picture grew heavier in the same audit. That is exactly what our Pass 1 forensic review uncovered.

book_subsections.title: Why We Trimmed Base Fair Value from ₹400.00 to ₹360.00
paragraphs: Flip the valuation lens upside down and run a Reverse DCF on ₹268.10 to ₹277.00. In our prior report, we added September 2026 gross debt of ₹119 Cr to equity value. From the verbatim October 22, 2026 Q2 FY27 earnings call transcript, we now know management plans ~₹110 Cr of H2 FY27 capex and will draw the remaining ~₹50 Cr seamless-tube term loan, pushing gross debt to roughly ₹165–170 Cr by March 2027. Adding that projected debt puts forward enterprise value near ₹1,955 Cr. At a 12.5% cost of capital and 5% terminal growth rate, today’s price still assumes 14% to 16% annual revenue compounding through FY32, EBITDA margins expanding from 12.06% toward 14.5%–15.0%, and working capital falling back below 95 days.

Three Pass 1 discoveries force us to shave our FY28E profit forecast and exit multiple. First, H1 FY27 unaudited operating cash flow collapsed to just ₹4.73 Cr on ₹33.16 Cr of net profit—a 14.3% conversion rate—after Other Current Assets jumped ₹23.89 Cr to ₹54.32 Cr, producing -₹54.43 Cr of H1 free cash flow on top of -₹111 Cr across FY24–FY26. Second, the October 30, 2026 preferential allotment brought only ₹39.75 Cr in upfront cash (₹31.80 Cr from non-promoter shares plus ₹7.95 Cr from the 25% promoter warrant deposit), leaving ₹23.85 Cr contingent on 18-month warrant conversion across 6.75 Cr fully diluted shares while management also adds a new ₹20–25 Cr Cold Drawn Tube line in Jamshedpur. Third, Mill 219 is a 1,20,000 TPA facility—not 40,000 TPA—meaning roughly 60,000 TPA of non-captive output must be sold into Oil & Gas and general engineering against a 93%-share domestic oligopoly of Maharashtra Seamless, Jindal SAW, and Kirloskar Ferrous (ISMT).

Reflecting higher FY28 interest expense on ~₹165–170 Cr peak debt, higher depreciation from the Cold Drawn Tube line, and a slower external Oil & Gas ramp, we trim our Base Case FY28E PAT from ₹108 Cr to ₹101 Cr—or ₹14.96 per diluted share across 6.75 Cr shares. Applying a 24.0x exit P/E (trimmed from 25.0x) produces our revised Base Case target of ₹360.00. In our Bull Case, clean Mill 219 commissioning and a notified DGTR anti-dumping duty lift FY28E PAT to ₹112 Cr (₹16.59 EPS) at 26.5x, yielding ₹440.00. In our Bear Case, freight slows or external tube sales stall under ~₹170 Cr peak debt, holding FY28E PAT to ₹78 Cr (₹11.56 EPS) at 15.5x—producing ₹180.00.

book_subsections.title: Benchmarking Kross Against Live Peer Multiples
paragraphs: Place Kross next to its four verified Indian commercial-vehicle and forging peers on the November 25, 2026 TradingView tape, and our 24.0x Base Case ceiling makes immediate sense. Jamna Auto Industries trades at 21.70x trailing earnings with a 22.48% ROE, virtually zero leverage (0.01x debt-to-equity), and a 12.81% operating margin. GNA Axles trades at 15.49x trailing earnings with a 14.40% ROE, 0.19x debt-to-equity, and +23.06% trailing revenue growth. At the other extreme, Ramkrishna Forgings trades at 73.46x earnings on a compressed 8.69% operating margin, while Bharat Forge sits in Stage 4 markdown at 121.51x earnings after a 36.88% EPS decline.

Notice the trade-off embedded in Kross’s 24.91x multiple at ₹268.10. You are paying a 15% P/E premium over Jamna Auto and a 61% premium over GNA Axles for Kross’s faster top-line growth (+35.86% TTM revenue, +40.17% TTM EPS) and its trailer-axle expansion. That premium is defensible only if captive Mill 219 integration lifts operating margins by 125 to 150 basis points and stops the cash-flow bleed.

Now check the reward-to-risk arithmetic against our ratcheted hard stop at ₹219.06. On the November 23, 2026 NSE ledger close of ₹277.00, Base Case upside to ₹360.00 is ₹83.00 against ₹57.94 of downside to ₹219.06—a reward-to-risk ratio of just 1.43 to 1, below our 1.50 to 1 hurdle. Even after the drop to ₹268.10 on November 25 (where raw asymmetry improves to 1.87 to 1), catching a stock sliding below its 50-day moving average with 14.3% H1 cash conversion is premature. Waiting for structural support at ₹234.00–₹252.00 stretches Base Case asymmetry to 3.28 to 1 from ₹252.00, giving you a true margin of safety for Mill 219 execution risk.

Look back at our GNA Axles historical parallel from 2018 to 2020. When a cyclical auto ancillary carries fresh capacity into a freight slowdown, earnings and P/E multiples compress simultaneously. Anchoring our Bear Case at 15.5x—right on top of GNA Axles’ live 15.49x valuation—reminds us that ₹180.00 is a realistic downside floor if truck volumes cool while Kross carries ₹165–170 Cr of gross debt. Disciplined buyers never pay upfront for a 1,20,000 TPA seamless-tube ramp that has not yet survived its first quarter of commercial trials.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: Cheaper Price, Heavier Balance Sheet
book_callouts.quote: A 12.5% pullback only widens your margin of safety if the balance sheet did not quietly add ₹50 Cr of upcoming debt and lose ₹54 Cr of free cash flow in the meantime.
book_callouts.text: Trimming our Base Target from ₹400.00 to ₹360.00 honors the Pass 1 forensics—14.3% H1 CFO/PAT conversion, ~₹165–170 Cr projected March 2027 debt, and the 93% seamless-tube oligopoly—while preserving a 3.28:1 asymmetric setup if price tests ₹234.00–₹252.00.
